mcqs.question: A sealed container of an ideal gas is heated at constant volume and 500 J of heat is supplied to the system. Which statement correctly describes the change in internal energy of the gas?

options.A: The internal energy increases by 500 J.
options.B: The internal energy decreases by 500 J.
options.D: The internal energy increases by 0 J.

mcqs.answer: The internal energy increases by 500 J.
mcqs.explanation: At constant volume no work is done (w = 0). According to the first law, ΔU = q + w = q. Hence the internal energy of the gas increases by the amount of heat supplied, i.e., 500 J. Options B, C and D contradict the first‑law relationship.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate internal energy to heat and work
mcqs.question: In a process, 300 J of heat is added to a gas which expands and does 120 J of work on the surroundings. What is the net change in internal energy of the gas?
mcqs.explanation: Using the first law ΔU = q + w, where w is work done on the system. Here the gas does work on the surroundings, so w = –120 J. Thus ΔU = 300 J + (‑120 J) = 180 J. Option A gives the opposite sign, C ignores work, and D adds work instead of subtracting it.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines the internal energy of a system?

options.A: It is the sum of the kinetic and potential energies of all the molecules in the system.
options.B: It is the same as the temperature of the system.
options.C: It is only the kinetic energy of the molecules.
options.D: It is the energy associated with the macroscopic motion of the system.

mcqs.answer: It is the sum of the kinetic and potential energies of all the molecules in the system.
mcqs.explanation: Internal energy (U) comprises all microscopic kinetic (translational, rotational, vibrational) and potential (inter‑molecular) energies of the particles. It is not identical to temperature (B), nor limited to kinetic energy alone (C), and does not include macroscopic kinetic or potential energy of the whole system (D).

mcqs.question: A system does 200 J of work on its surroundings and no heat is exchanged with the environment. What is the change in internal energy of the system?

options.A: The internal energy increases by 200 J.
options.B: The internal energy decreases by 200 J.
options.C: There is no change in internal energy.
options.D: The internal energy increases by 0 J.

mcqs.answer: The internal energy decreases by 200 J.
mcqs.explanation: With q = 0 (no heat) and work done by the system w = +200 J, the first law gives ΔU = q – w = –200 J (or ΔU = q + w_on_system = 0 – 200 J). Hence the internal energy drops by 200 J. Options A, C, and D are inconsistent with the sign convention.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate internal energy to heat and work
mcqs.question: Two identical gases receive the same amount of heat (400 J). Process (i) is carried out at constant pressure, while process (ii) is at constant volume. Which statement correctly compares the changes in internal energy (ΔU) and work done (w) in the two processes?

options.A: ΔU is the same for both processes, and work done is larger in process (i).
options.B: ΔU is larger in process (i), while work done is the same in both processes.
options.C: ΔU is the same for both processes, and work done is zero in both processes.
options.D: ΔU is larger in process (ii), and work done is larger in process (i).

mcqs.answer: ΔU is larger in process (ii), and work done is larger in process (i).
mcqs.explanation: At constant volume (process ii) no work is performed, so ΔU = q = 400 J. At constant pressure (process i) part of the heat is used for expansion work, so ΔU = q – w < 400 J. Therefore internal energy increase is greater in the constant‑volume case, while work done is greater (non‑zero) in the constant‑pressure case. Options A, B, and C misrepresent either ΔU or work.

mcqs.question: The internal energy of a system is best described as:

options.A: The sum of kinetic energies of all the molecules only.
options.B: The sum of potential energies of all the molecules only.
options.C: The sum of kinetic and potential energies of all the molecules.
options.D: The energy associated with the macroscopic motion of the system.

mcqs.answer: The sum of kinetic and potential energies of all the molecules.
mcqs.explanation: Internal energy (U) includes both microscopic kinetic (translational, rotational, vibrational) and potential (inter‑molecular) energies of the particles. Options A and B consider only one component, while D refers to macroscopic kinetic or potential energy, which is not part of internal energy.

mcqs.question: Which of the following processes will increase the internal energy of an ideal gas?

options.C: Keeping the gas at constant volume with no heat exchange.
options.D: Cooling the gas at constant pressure.

mcqs.explanation: In adiabatic compression work is done on the system (w positive), and since q = 0, ΔU = w > 0, raising internal energy. In adiabatic expansion work is done by the system, decreasing U (B). Options C and D involve no work input or removal of heat, leading to no increase or a decrease in U.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate internal energy to heat and work
mcqs.question: According to the first law of thermodynamics (as used in chemistry), which equation correctly relates the change in internal energy (ΔU) to heat (q) and work (w) when work is defined as work done on the system?
mcqs.explanation: In chemistry the sign convention takes work done on the system as positive. Therefore the first law is written as ΔU = q + w. Option A uses the physics convention (work done by the system), while C and D ignore one of the energy terms.
